subject: physical-education
unitTitle: Access, Cost, Facilities, and Community Resources
essentialQuestion: What does it actually cost to stay active, and what costs nothing?

prompts.prompt: Explain the critical features or key principle of the real cost of gyms, clubs, leagues, and equipment in your own words.
Demonstrate or fully describe free and low-cost public activity infrastructure using a version your body and setting allow. A described or adapted version earns full credit.
Apply contracts, memberships, and cancellation terms in a new situation and explain the decision or adjustment you made.
Analyze a plausible technique fault, tactical error, or unsafe choice involving community, workplace, and campus activity options; correct it and explain why.
Connect transport and time as the binding constraints with building an activity life on a small budget and explain how one affects the other.

Present the strongest evidence from the unit task: Produce an access plan comparing at least three ways to stay active after graduation on different budgets, including one that costs nothing, and identify the failure point of each.
Identify one thing you can now do or direct yourself, one adjustment that improved it, and one next goal you set for yourself.

adaptationChoices: The comparison may be written, tabled, or spoken; publicly available information is supplied if the learner cannot research independently.
accommodationNote: Access supports may change format, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, setting, or response mode without changing the standard being assessed. An adapted or described performance is full credit, not partial credit.
neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
